title: Hourly to Annual Pay: How Australia's Minimum Wage Compares to the Minimum Wage in America
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual salary using the 38-hour week. See how Australia's $26.44 National Minimum Wage compares to the minimum wage in America, plus tax and super.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is hourly × 38 × 52. The National Minimum Wage of $26.44/hour gives $52,224.72 per year before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual pay?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by hours per week (assume 38 if not stated) and then by 52. For example, $30/hour × 38 × 52 = $59,280 gross per year. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of leave entitlements. The National Minimum Wage for casuals is $33.05/hour (base $26.44 + 25%). When using the timesheet, tick the casual loading checkbox – never type a rate that already includes it.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on my annual earnings?
faqs.a: Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary-time earnings, paid on top of your gross pay. For example, on a $60,000 annual salary, super adds $7,200 per year, but only up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it's an extra contribution by your employer.

bodyMarkdown:
## From Hourly to Annual: Understanding Your Pay in Australia

If you're paid by the hour or considering a salary offer, converting between hourly and annual pay is essential. The standard formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. In Australia, most full-time roles assume a 38 hours per week, so we use that unless your award or contract says otherwise. This gives you the gross annual gross figure before tax and super.

### How the Formula Works

Let's say you earn $30 per hour. Multiply 30 × 38 = $1,140 per week. Multiply that by 52 weeks gives $59,290 per year. That's your gross annual pay before any tax or super. If you want your fortnightly (fortnightly) pay, just multiply weekly by 2: $2,280 per fortnight.

But remember: this formula assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It's a baseline estimate.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. That's the legal floor set by the Fair Work Commission. However, most employees are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that pays more. Award rates vary by industry and job classification, so check your specific award on the Fair Work Ombudsman website. The National Minimum Wage is not a job median; it's the minimum for award-free employees.

Casual employees get an extra 25% loading on top of the base rate. For the National Minimum Wage, that's $33.05 per hour. When you use [the timesheet](/), tick the casual loading checkbox – never type a rate that already includes casual loading.

### How Australia Compares to the Minimum Wage in America

It's interesting to see how Australia's minimum wage stacks up against the minimum wage in America. The US federal minimum wage remains $7.25 per hour – that's about $10.50 Australian dollars at current exchange rates. Even after converting, Australia's $26.44 is more than double. But that's not the whole story. The minimum wage in America varies by state; some states like California or Washington have rates above $15 per hour. Still, Australia's National Minimum Wage is among the highest in the world, and when you add superannuation (12% on top), the total compensation is even higher.

However, the cost of living and tax systems differ. In Australia, the tax-free threshold is $18,200, and Medicare levy is 2%. In the US, federal income tax starts at 10% but state taxes vary. The minimum wage in America is often debated, but in Australia, the Fair Work Commission reviews the minimum wage annually.

### Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS), average weekly earnings for full-time adult ordinary time employees were $2,083.70 in May 2026. That's an average across all industries and states, not a median for a specific job. For all employees (including part-time), total earnings averaged $1,579.20 per week. These figures show that many Australians earn well above the minimum wage.

When comparing to the minimum wage in America, the average US weekly earnings for full-time workers are around $1,100 (USD) – but again, that's an average, not a median. The gap in ordinary-time earnings reflects different labour market structures and award systems.

### Tax and Superannuation

Once you have your annual gross pay, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus Medicare levy of 2% (single reduction thresholds from 2025–26 used here as 2026–27 not confirmed). This is an estimate, not a determination of your tax.

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary-time earnings, paid on top by your employer. For example, on a $60,000 salary, super adds $7,200 per year, but only up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it's an extra contribution. You can learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) and [take-home pay](/topics/take-home).

### Using the Timesheet

To convert your own hourly rate, go to [the timesheet](/). Type your base hourly rate, and if you're casual, tick the casual loading checkbox. The timesheet will show weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay. It also estimates tax and super using the rates above. Remember: the timesheet assumes a 38-hour week unless you change it.

For more detailed pay guides, see [pay guides](/blog). For reference tables, see [reference tables](/data). And for information on award rates, see [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage).

### Final Notes

This article is a guide only. Your actual pay may differ due to awards, agreements, overtime, penalties, or salary packaging. Always check your pay slip and consult the Fair Work Ombudsman if unsure. The minimum wage in America is just one comparison; Australia's system provides a strong safety net with regular reviews.

Remember: the formula is hourly × hours per week × 52. Use 38 hours unless you know otherwise. And super is on top, not included in your hourly rate.
